title: Correlation and Regression
summary: Correlation meaning and strength; scatter plot; Pearson's r; simple linear regression; point-biserial; biserial; phi; tetrachoric; Spearman rank; Kendall's tau.
objectives: Define correlation and interpret r values.
Distinguish Pearson, Spearman, Kendall, point-biserial, phi and tetrachoric.
Use scatter plots and simple linear regression.
revision: Correlation −1 to +1; Pearson continuous, Spearman ranks, Phi dichotomous. Regression predicts (Y = a + bX). Correlation ≠ causation.
traps: r = 0 means no linear relationship, not no relationship at all.

notes.t: A statistical technique that measures the strength and direction of the relationship between two or more variables. Correlation ranges from −1.00 to +1.00.

A scatter plot graphs pairs of scores to visually show the direction, form and strength of a relationship. Points rising left-to-right = positive correlation; falling = negative; no pattern = zero correlation.
A method for predicting scores on one variable (Y) from scores on another (X) using a linear equation.
Regression equation: Y = a + bX, where a is the intercept and b is the slope. Regression predicts; correlation describes relationship.

Worked example: r = 0.85 between study hours (X) and exam score (Y).
Interpretation: Strong positive correlation — more study hours associated with higher scores.
Regression: if a = 50 and b = 5, then for X = 6 hours, Y = 50 + 5(6) = 80.
Correlation ≠ causation. Pearson's r for continuous × continuous; Spearman for ranks; Phi for dichotomous × dichotomous. Frequently matched in UGC NET.
